html:
In the app

File → New Project… → Card Sort Cell opens the cell in Automatic, with its tags made and an empty routine. Guided → New Guided Project: Card Sort Cell… opens it with Card motion on PLC, the two modules and the tags, and walks through the program below a routine at a time. File → Load Reference Solution: Card Sort Cell loads the whole program into the cell that is open.

The Card Sort Cell is the bench fixture for Level 11’s camera cards, modelled on a real one: a baseboard with a red fixture on it, holding a magazine of the eighteen Level 11 cards on a grip ramp, a nest under a ring light, and a PASS tray and a FAIL tray; a copy stand with an In-Sight camera (Vision_1, module Cam1) and a DataMan code reader (Code_1, module Reader1) over the nest; a push button, PASS and FAIL lamps, a TCP socket and an HMI. Vision_1 judges the card in the nest (cap, label, fill, and the lot code against the lot it was told), Code_1 reads its serial, and the cell keeps a tally against the answer key. The 3D view shows it at its real size on a bench.

How the cards move

The cell’s Card motion setting decides who moves the cards. By hand: in Run mode, click the magazine to feed the next card and a tray to sort it. Automatic (the default in the New Project card): the cell feeds the next card when the nest is empty and sorts the card in the nest on the camera’s result, code 0 to PASS and anything else to FAIL. PLC: the cell gives the program three outputs, Feed, Sort_Pass and Sort_Fail (each acts on its rising edge), and a Pusher_Home input. A feed is the pusher: the block at the end of the ramp runs out to the magazine in half a second, carrying the bottom card into the nest, and goes home. A sort answers with a pulse, Sorted_Pass or Sorted_Fail, as the card leaves the nest.

The program

The reference program runs the cell with Card motion on PLC. One step register carries each card through the cycle: 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort, and back to 10. Each routine acts only in its own steps, so MainRoutine is just the index.

Lamp_FailBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.1FAIL lamp

Sort_FailBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.6The cell: rising edge sorts it to FAIL
Sorted_PassBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.2Pulse: a card went into the PASS tray
Sorted_FailBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.3Pulse: a card went into the FAIL tray

Start and feed

Push_1 starts a cycle, once, on its edge, and clears the counts. In step 10, with the nest empty, a timer gives the last card 0.6 s to land in its tray; then Feed, with the pusher home, carries the bottom card into the nest. The card in: count it, forget the last card’s handshakes, and move on to step 20. The cycle ends when the magazine is empty, the nest clear and the pusher home. That last condition matters: while the pusher is out with the eighteenth card the magazine is already empty and the nest still clear, and without it the cycle would end with a card in transit.

The lot over TCP

The camera judges each card’s lot code against the lot it was told, so it has to be told before the picture. The magazine holds the three lots in order, six cards each, so LIM finds the lot from the card number. A new lot goes into the socket’s SendValue (TCP_Lot) and is sent as LOT n on a rising edge of TCP_Send, held 0.2 s by a timer. Then the card settles for 0.3 s and the step moves on to the picture. With the socket down the cycle waits here, which is what it should do.

Two triggers, 250 ms apart

Both readers look into the nest, and each has its own light. So the camera goes first and the DataMan 250 ms after it, once the camera’s light is off. Each trigger is the handshake from Level 8 (chapter 40): latch Trigger when the reader is ready, drop it on Trigger_Ack. A flag per reader (Cam_Fired, DM_Fired) makes it once per card.

The results, and the cross-check

Each reader’s result is taken while it is offered, then acknowledged. From the camera: its result code, and the card ID in byte 10 of Inspection_Results. From the DataMan: its result code, and the serial it read, copied into a STRING (the bytes into DATA with COP, the count into LEN). The serial’s last character is the card ID too: SN-4801 is card 1, since '1' is 49 and 49 less 48 is 1. If the reader read nothing, or the two disagree on which card this is, the cross-check fails and the card can’t pass. PASS needs code 0 and the cross-check good. The lamps show the last card’s verdict.

Sort, count, and the next card

In step 50 the verdict picks the output, Sort_Pass or Sort_Fail, on its rising edge. The cell answers with Sorted_Pass or Sorted_Fail as the card leaves the nest: count it and go back to step 10 for the next card. A full magazine runs in a little over a minute at 4×, and the tally under the board should read 18 right.

What to break on purpose

Shuffle the magazine (the cell’s Magazine order) and run again: the lots no longer come six at a time, and the wrong-lot results show it. Dirty the DataMan’s window (Machine Faults → Code reader window dirty): every read is a no read, and the cross-check sends every card to FAIL. Stop the socket (its Host set to an address nobody answers): the cycle waits in step 20 for the lot. With a real 5603 and DataMan, their modules set to Implicit I/O, the same rungs run the bench.

Try it

Run the cell in Automatic first and watch the tally build up, so you know what right looks like. Then start Guided → New Guided Project: Card Sort Cell… and write the five routines one at a time, running after each; the guide checks each one in Run mode.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE INDEX: the feed, the lot, the inspection, the results, the sort. Each routine acts on its own value of Step
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine CC_Feed.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(CC_Feed) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine CC_Feed. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.
pats.think: a running order on a clipboard: the main routine reads it top to bottom, and each line sends you to a page that does one job.
pats.watch: A new routine does nothing until a JSR calls it. If a routine’s rungs never highlight online, look here first.

rungs.head: CC_Feed · Rung 0
rungs.comment: START: Push_1 starts a cycle with cards in the magazine. The counts and the lot sent start over
rungs.words: When Push_1 (Push button) is on, Cycle_On (The cycle is running: Push_1 starts it, the empty magazine ends it) is off, Mag_Empty (The magazine is empty) is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Cycle_On on, clears Card_No (Cards fed this cycle: card 1 is the first) to 0, clears Lot_Sent (The lot the camera was last sent) to 0, clears Pass_Count (Cards sorted to PASS this cycle) to 0, clears Fail_Count (Cards sorted to FAIL this cycle) to 0, clears Mismatches (Cards the cross-check failed) to 0, unlatches Has_Res (A card has been judged: the lamps show the last verdict) and puts 10 into Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Push_1) Examine If Closed asks: true when Push_1 is on.
  2. XIO(Cycle_On) Examine If Open asks: true when Cycle_On is off.
  3. XIO(Mag_Empty) Examine If Open asks: true when Mag_Empty is off.
  4. ONS(Start_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Start_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  5. A branch of 8 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Cycle_On) Output Latch does: latches Cycle_On on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. CLR(Card_No) Clear does: clears Card_No to 0.
    Path 3
    1. CLR(Lot_Sent) Clear does: clears Lot_Sent to 0.
    Path 4
    1. CLR(Pass_Count) Clear does: clears Pass_Count to 0.
    Path 5
    1. CLR(Fail_Count) Clear does: clears Fail_Count to 0.
    Path 6
    1. CLR(Mismatches) Clear does: clears Mismatches to 0.
    Path 7
    1. OTU(Has_Res) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Has_Res. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 8
    1. MOV(10,Step) Move does: puts 10 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: Cycle_On stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: CC_Feed · Rung 1
rungs.comment: FEED WAIT: the nest is empty; give the last card 0.6 s to land in its tray (the pusher won't move while a card is still sliding)

pred.q: Cycle_On is on, Card_In_Nest is off, Mag_Empty is off and Step is 10. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Feed_T times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Cycle_On (The cycle is running: Push_1 starts it, the empty magazine ends it) is on, Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 10, Card_In_Nest (A card is in the nest) is off and Mag_Empty (The magazine is empty) is off, the rung runs the timer Feed_T (Feed wait: the last card lands in its tray before the next is fed) toward 600 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cycle_On) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cycle_On is on.
  2. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIO(Card_In_Nest) Examine If Open asks: true when Card_In_Nest is off.
  4. XIO(Mag_Empty) Examine If Open asks: true when Mag_Empty is off.
  5. TON(Feed_T,600,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Feed_T toward 600 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Feed_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: CC_Feed · Rung 2
rungs.comment: FEED: the pusher runs on the rising edge and carries the bottom card into the nest. Feed drops as the pusher leaves home

pred.q: Feed_T.DN is off, Pusher_Home is off and Card_In_Nest is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Feed is off. It stops at XIC(Feed_T.DN).

rungs.words: When Feed_T.DN (the done bit of Feed_T: Feed wait: the last card lands in its tray before the next is fed) is on, Pusher_Home (The cell: the feeder pusher is home) is on and Card_In_Nest (A card is in the nest) is off, the rung turns Feed (The cell: rising edge feeds the next card) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Feed_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Feed_T.DN is on.
  2. XIC(Pusher_Home) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pusher_Home is on.
  3. XIO(Card_In_Nest) Examine If Open asks: true when Card_In_Nest is off.
  4. OTE(Feed) Output Energize does: turns Feed on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Feed · Rung 3
rungs.comment: CARD IN: count it, forget the last card's handshakes, on to the lot
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 10 and Card_In_Nest (A card is in the nest) is on, the rung makes Card_No (Cards fed this cycle: card 1 is the first) = Card_No + 1, unlatches Cam_Fired (The camera has been triggered for this card), unlatches DM_Fired (The DataMan has been triggered for this card), unlatches Cam_Got (The camera's result for this card is in), unlatches DM_Got (The DataMan's result for this card is in) and puts 20 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Card_In_Nest) Examine If Closed asks: true when Card_In_Nest is on.
  3. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Card_No,1,Card_No) Add does: makes Card_No = Card_No + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Cam_Fired) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam_Fired. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(DM_Fired) Output Unlatch does: unlatches DM_Fired. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTU(Cam_Got) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam_Got. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 5
    1. OTU(DM_Got) Output Unlatch does: unlatches DM_Got. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 6
    1. MOV(20,Step) Move does: puts 20 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 10, to 20); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: CC_Feed · Rung 4
rungs.comment: DONE: the magazine is empty, the last card sorted, and the pusher home (it is out while the last card rides into the nest)

pred.q: Cycle_On is on, Mag_Empty is on, Card_In_Nest is off, Pusher_Home is on and Step is 10. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cycle_On is unlatched and Step is written.

rungs.words: When Cycle_On (The cycle is running: Push_1 starts it, the empty magazine ends it) is on, Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 10, Mag_Empty (The magazine is empty) is on, Card_In_Nest (A card is in the nest) is off and Pusher_Home (The cell: the feeder pusher is home) is on, the rung unlatches Cycle_On and puts 0 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cycle_On) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cycle_On is on.
  2. EQU(Step,10) Equal asks: true when Step equals 10. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIC(Mag_Empty) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mag_Empty is on.
  4. XIO(Card_In_Nest) Examine If Open asks: true when Card_In_Nest is off.
  5. XIC(Pusher_Home) Examine If Closed asks: true when Pusher_Home is on.
  6. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cycle_On) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cycle_On. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(0,Step) Move does: puts 0 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 10, to 0); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE LOT this card belongs to: the magazine holds the three lots in order, six cards each

pred.q: Step is 19 and Card_No is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lot_Want is not written (it keeps its value), Lot_Want is not written (it keeps its value) and Lot_Want is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at EQU(Step,20).

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 20, each path is tested on its own: if Card_No (Cards fed this cycle: card 1 is the first) is between 1 and 6, it puts 101 into Lot_Want (The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18); if Card_No is between 7 and 12, it puts 102 into Lot_Want; if Card_No is between 13 and 18, it puts 103 into Lot_Want.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. LIM(1,Card_No,6) Limit Test asks: true when Card_No is between 1 and 6. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(101,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 101 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. LIM(7,Card_No,12) Limit Test asks: true when Card_No is between 7 and 12. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(102,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 102 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. LIM(13,Card_No,18) Limit Test asks: true when Card_No is between 13 and 18. The test is inclusive at both ends.
    2. MOV(103,Lot_Want) Move does: puts 103 into Lot_Want. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.
pats.think: meeting a train. You cannot stand at one exact inch of track and wait for it to stop there; you watch the whole platform.
pats.watch: An EQU on a measured value (a position, a level, a weight) may never be true: the value jumps from just under to just over between scans.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 1
rungs.comment: A new lot: put it in the socket's SendValue
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 20 and Lot_Want (The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18) is not Lot_Sent (The lot the camera was last sent), the rung puts Lot_Want into TCP_Lot (TCP: the lot number sent as LOT n).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. NEQ(Lot_Want,Lot_Sent) Not Equal asks: true when Lot_Want is not Lot_Sent.
  3. MOV(Lot_Want,TCP_Lot) Move does: puts Lot_Want into TCP_Lot. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 2
rungs.comment: …and with the socket connected, send it: TCP_Send on for 0.2 s

pred.q: TCP_Connected is on, Step is 20, Lot_Want is 18 and Lot_Sent is 22. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Send_T times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 20, Lot_Want (The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18) is not Lot_Sent (The lot the camera was last sent) and TCP_Connected (TCP: connection up) is on, the rung runs the timer Send_T (Holds TCP_Send on for 0.2 s) toward 200 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. NEQ(Lot_Want,Lot_Sent) Not Equal asks: true when Lot_Want is not Lot_Sent.
  3. XIC(TCP_Connected) Examine If Closed asks: true when TCP_Connected is on.
  4. TON(Send_T,200,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Send_T toward 200 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Send_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 3
rungs.comment: SEND: the socket sends LOT n on the rising edge
rungs.words: When Send_T.TT (the timing bit of Send_T: Holds TCP_Send on for 0.2 s) is on, the rung turns TCP_Send (TCP: rising edge sends LOT {SendValue} to the camera) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Send_T.TT) Examine If Closed asks: true when Send_T.TT is on.
  2. OTE(TCP_Send) Output Energize does: turns TCP_Send on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Sent: the camera now judges the lot code against this lot

pred.q: Send_T.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lot_Sent is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Send_T.DN).

rungs.words: When Send_T.DN (the done bit of Send_T: Holds TCP_Send on for 0.2 s) is on, the rung puts Lot_Want (The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18) into Lot_Sent (The lot the camera was last sent).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Send_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Send_T.DN is on.
  2. MOV(Lot_Want,Lot_Sent) Move does: puts Lot_Want into Lot_Sent. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 5
rungs.comment: SETTLE: the lot is set; let the card settle in the nest for 0.3 s
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 20 and Lot_Sent (The lot the camera was last sent) equals Lot_Want (The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18), the rung runs the timer Settle_T (The card settles in the nest before the picture) toward 300 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,20) Equal asks: true when Step equals 20. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. EQU(Lot_Sent,Lot_Want) Equal asks: true when Lot_Sent equals Lot_Want. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. TON(Settle_T,300,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Settle_T toward 300 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Settle_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: CC_Lot · Rung 6
rungs.comment: …then the picture

pred.q: Settle_T.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Settle_T.DN (the done bit of Settle_T: The card settles in the nest before the picture) is on, the rung puts 30 into Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort).

1. XIC(Settle_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Settle_T.DN is on.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE TWO READERS: the camera and the DataMan may be triggered; the camera's results are buffered
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. OTE(Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Reader1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 1
rungs.comment: TRIGGER THE CAMERA once per card, when it is ready

pred.q: Cam_Fired is off, Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is off and Step is 30. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger is left as it was and Cam_Fired is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready).

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 30, Cam_Fired (The camera has been triggered for this card) is off and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on and latches Cam_Fired on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,30) Equal asks: true when Step equals 30. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIO(Cam_Fired) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam_Fired is off.
  3. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam_Fired) Output Latch does: latches Cam_Fired on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 2
rungs.comment: …Trigger_Ack: drop the trigger

pred.q: Cam1:O.Trigger is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Cam1:O.Trigger is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Cam1:O.Trigger is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:O.Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:O.Trigger is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  3. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE DATAMAN 250 MS LATER: the camera's light is off by then
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 30 and Cam_Fired (The camera has been triggered for this card) is on, the rung runs the timer DM_Delay (The DataMan goes 250 ms after the camera) toward 250 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,30) Equal asks: true when Step equals 30. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Cam_Fired) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam_Fired is on.
  3. TON(DM_Delay,250,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer DM_Delay toward 250 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: DM_Delay counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 4
rungs.comment: TRIGGER THE DATAMAN once per card

pred.q: DM_Delay.DN is off, DM_Fired is off and Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Reader1:O.Trigger is left as it was and DM_Fired is left as it was. It stops at XIC(DM_Delay.DN).

rungs.words: When DM_Delay.DN (the done bit of DM_Delay: The DataMan goes 250 ms after the camera) is on, DM_Fired (The DataMan has been triggered for this card) is off and Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Reader1:O.Trigger on and latches DM_Fired on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(DM_Delay.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when DM_Delay.DN is on.
  2. XIO(DM_Fired) Examine If Open asks: true when DM_Fired is off.
  3. XIC(Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  4. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Reader1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Reader1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(DM_Fired) Output Latch does: latches DM_Fired on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Reader1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 5
rungs.comment: …Trigger_Ack: drop it
rungs.words: When Reader1:O.Trigger is on and Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Reader1:O.Trigger.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reader1:O.Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:O.Trigger is on.
  2. XIC(Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  3. OTU(Reader1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reader1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Reader1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: CC_Inspect · Rung 6
rungs.comment: Both triggered: wait for the results

pred.q: DM_Fired is on and Step is 30. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 30 and DM_Fired (The DataMan has been triggered for this card) is on, the rung puts 40 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,30) Equal asks: true when Step equals 30. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(DM_Fired) Examine If Closed asks: true when DM_Fired is on.
  3. MOV(40,Step) Move does: puts 40 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 30, to 40); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE CAMERA'S RESULT: the code, and the card ID from byte 10; then acknowledge

pred.q: Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam_Code is not written (it keeps its value), Cam_Card is not written (it keeps its value), Cam_Got is left as it was and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack).

rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Cam_Code (The camera's result code: 0 pass; 1 no cap, 2 no label, 4 short fill, 32 wrong lot, 64 no code), puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[10] into Cam_Card (The card ID the camera found (byte 10): 1-4, SN-4801 to SN-4804), latches Cam_Got (The camera's result for this card is in) on and latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Cam_Code) Move does: puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into Cam_Code. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[10],Cam_Card) Move does: puts Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[10] into Cam_Card. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. OTL(Cam_Got) Output Latch does: latches Cam_Got on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam_Got stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 1
rungs.comment: …drop the ack once Results_Valid has gone
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 2
rungs.comment: THE DATAMAN'S RESULT: the code, and the SN into a STRING (the bytes into DATA, the length into LEN); then acknowledge
rungs.words: When Reader1:I.Results_Available is on and Reader1:O.Results_Ack is off, the rung puts Reader1:I.Result_Code into DM_Result (The DataMan's Result_Code: bit 0 a code was read), copies 16 elements from Reader1:I.Result_Data[0] to Code_Text.DATA[0] (The SN the DataMan read), puts Reader1:I.Result_Length into Code_Text.LEN (the length of Code_Text: The SN the DataMan read), latches DM_Got (The DataMan's result for this card is in) on and latches Reader1:O.Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reader1:I.Results_Available) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reader1:I.Results_Available is on.
  2. XIO(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Reader1:O.Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 5 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(Reader1:I.Result_Code,DM_Result) Move does: puts Reader1:I.Result_Code into DM_Result. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. COP(Reader1:I.Result_Data[0],Code_Text.DATA[0],16) Copy File does: copies 16 elements from Reader1:I.Result_Data[0] to Code_Text.DATA[0].
    Path 3
    1. MOV(Reader1:I.Result_Length,Code_Text.LEN) Move does: puts Reader1:I.Result_Length into Code_Text.LEN. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(DM_Got) Output Latch does: latches DM_Got on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 5
    1. OTL(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Reader1:O.Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: DM_Got stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 3
rungs.comment: …drop its ack
rungs.words: When Reader1:I.Results_Available is off, the rung unlatches Reader1:O.Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Reader1:I.Results_Available) Examine If Open asks: true when Reader1:I.Results_Available is off.
  2. OTU(Reader1:O.Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reader1:O.Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Reader1:O.Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 4
rungs.comment: BOTH IN: the card ID in the SN is its last character (SN-4801: '1' is 49, less 48 is 1)

pred.q: Cam_Got is on, DM_Got is on and Step is 40. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: DM_Card is written, Cross_Fail is unlatched, Verdict_Pass is unlatched, Has_Res latches on and Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 40, Cam_Got (The camera's result for this card is in) is on and DM_Got (The DataMan's result for this card is in) is on, the rung makes DM_Card (The card ID in the SN the DataMan read (its last digit)) = Code_Text.DATA[6] (The SN the DataMan read) − 48, unlatches Cross_Fail (The reader and the camera disagree on the card, or the reader read nothing), unlatches Verdict_Pass (This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good), latches Has_Res (A card has been judged: the lamps show the last verdict) on and puts 50 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,40) Equal asks: true when Step equals 40. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Cam_Got) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam_Got is on.
  3. XIC(DM_Got) Examine If Closed asks: true when DM_Got is on.
  4. A branch of 5 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. SUB(Code_Text.DATA[6],48,DM_Card) Subtract does: makes DM_Card = Code_Text.DATA[6] − 48. Every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Cross_Fail) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cross_Fail. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(Verdict_Pass) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Verdict_Pass. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. OTL(Has_Res) Output Latch does: latches Has_Res on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(50,Step) Move does: puts 50 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 40, to 50); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
Has_Res stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 5
rungs.comment: CROSS-CHECK: the reader read nothing, or the two disagree on which card this is
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50 and either (DM_Result.0 (The DataMan's Result_Code: bit 0 a code was read) is off) or (DM_Card (The card ID in the SN the DataMan read (its last digit)) is not Cam_Card (The card ID the camera found (byte 10): 1-4, SN-4801 to SN-4804)), the rung latches Cross_Fail (The reader and the camera disagree on the card, or the reader read nothing) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(DM_Result.0) Examine If Open asks: true when DM_Result.0 is off.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(DM_Card,Cam_Card) Not Equal asks: true when DM_Card is not Cam_Card.
  3. OTL(Cross_Fail) Output Latch does: latches Cross_Fail on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cross_Fail stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 6
rungs.comment: …counted
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50, Cross_Fail (The reader and the camera disagree on the card, or the reader read nothing) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Mismatches (Cards the cross-check failed) = Mismatches + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Cross_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cross_Fail is on.
  3. ONS(Cross_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cross_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. ADD(Mismatches,1,Mismatches) Add does: makes Mismatches = Mismatches + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 7
rungs.comment: THE VERDICT: PASS only on a clean result with the reader agreeing
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50, Cam_Code (The camera's result code: 0 pass; 1 no cap, 2 no label, 4 short fill, 32 wrong lot, 64 no code) equals 0 and Cross_Fail (The reader and the camera disagree on the card, or the reader read nothing) is off, the rung latches Verdict_Pass (This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. EQU(Cam_Code,0) Equal asks: true when Cam_Code equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIO(Cross_Fail) Examine If Open asks: true when Cross_Fail is off.
  4. OTL(Verdict_Pass) Output Latch does: latches Verdict_Pass on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Verdict_Pass stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 8
rungs.comment: THE LAMPS show the last card's verdict

pred.q: Has_Res is on and Verdict_Pass is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Pass is off. It stops at XIC(Verdict_Pass).

rungs.words: When Has_Res (A card has been judged: the lamps show the last verdict) is on and Verdict_Pass (This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Pass (PASS lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Has_Res) Examine If Closed asks: true when Has_Res is on.
  2. XIC(Verdict_Pass) Examine If Closed asks: true when Verdict_Pass is on.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Pass) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Pass on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Results · Rung 9
rungs.words: When Has_Res (A card has been judged: the lamps show the last verdict) is on and Verdict_Pass (This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good) is off, the rung turns Lamp_Fail (FAIL lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Has_Res) Examine If Closed asks: true when Has_Res is on.
  2. XIO(Verdict_Pass) Examine If Open asks: true when Verdict_Pass is off.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Fail) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fail on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pred.a: The rung is true: Sort_Pass is on.

  2. XIC(Verdict_Pass) Examine If Closed asks: true when Verdict_Pass is on.
  3. OTE(Sort_Pass) Output Energize does: turns Sort_Pass on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Sort · Rung 1
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50 and Verdict_Pass (This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good) is off, the rung turns Sort_Fail (The cell: rising edge sorts it to FAIL) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIO(Verdict_Pass) Examine If Open asks: true when Verdict_Pass is off.
  3. OTE(Sort_Fail) Output Energize does: turns Sort_Fail on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: CC_Sort · Rung 2
rungs.comment: SORTED: count it, on to the next card

pred.q: Sorted_Pass is off and Step is 50. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Pass_Count is not written (it keeps its value) and Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Sorted_Pass).

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50 and Sorted_Pass (Pulse: a card went into the PASS tray) is on, the rung makes Pass_Count (Cards sorted to PASS this cycle) = Pass_Count + 1 and puts 10 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Sorted_Pass) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sorted_Pass is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Pass_Count,1,Pass_Count) Add does: makes Pass_Count = Pass_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(10,Step) Move does: puts 10 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: CC_Sort · Rung 3
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort) equals 50 and Sorted_Fail (Pulse: a card went into the FAIL tray) is on, the rung makes Fail_Count (Cards sorted to FAIL this cycle) = Fail_Count + 1 and puts 10 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,50) Equal asks: true when Step equals 50. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Sorted_Fail) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sorted_Fail is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Fail_Count,1,Fail_Count) Add does: makes Fail_Count = Fail_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(10,Step) Move does: puts 10 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 50, to 10); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

Cycle_On.desc: The cycle is running: Push_1 starts it, the empty magazine ends it

Card_No.desc: Cards fed this cycle: card 1 is the first

Lot_Sent.desc: The lot the camera was last sent

Pass_Count.desc: Cards sorted to PASS this cycle

Fail_Count.desc: Cards sorted to FAIL this cycle

Has_Res.desc: A card has been judged: the lamps show the last verdict

Step.desc: The cycle step: 0 idle, 10 feed, 20 lot, 30 inspect, 40 results, 50 sort

Card_In_Nest.desc: A card is in the nest

Feed_T.desc: Feed wait: the last card lands in its tray before the next is fed

Pusher_Home.desc: The cell: the feeder pusher is home

Feed.desc: The cell: rising edge feeds the next card

Cam_Fired.desc: The camera has been triggered for this card

DM_Fired.desc: The DataMan has been triggered for this card

Cam_Got.desc: The camera's result for this card is in

DM_Got.desc: The DataMan's result for this card is in

Lot_Want.desc: The lot of the card in the nest: 101 for cards 1-6, 102 for 7-12, 103 for 13-18

TCP_Lot.desc: TCP: the lot number sent as LOT n

TCP_Send.desc: TCP: rising edge sends LOT {SendValue} to the camera

Settle_T.desc: The card settles in the nest before the picture

DM_Delay.desc: The DataMan goes 250 ms after the camera

Cam_Code.desc: The camera's result code: 0 pass; 1 no cap, 2 no label, 4 short fill, 32 wrong lot, 64 no code

Cam_Card.desc: The card ID the camera found (byte 10): 1-4, SN-4801 to SN-4804

DM_Result.desc: The DataMan's Result_Code: bit 0 a code was read

DM_Card.desc: The card ID in the SN the DataMan read (its last digit)

Cross_Fail.desc: The reader and the camera disagree on the card, or the reader read nothing

Verdict_Pass.desc: This card passes: camera code 0 and the cross-check good

Cross_ONS.desc: One-shot storage for the mismatch count

Sort_Pass.desc: The cell: rising edge sorts the card in the nest to PASS

Sort_Fail.desc: The cell: rising edge sorts it to FAIL

Sorted_Pass.desc: Pulse: a card went into the PASS tray

Sorted_Fail.desc: Pulse: a card went into the FAIL tray
